newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Stet Privatisation seen delayed.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Stet Privatisation seen delayed.

text.p: The sale of Italian state telecoms group Stet could be delayed until late 1997 at the earliest as government hopes of launching the privatisation by next March fade fast.
Milan business daily Il Sole 24 Ore said on Friday the delay of the sale until next October now looked inevitable.

The offering to the public of a 64 percent stake in Stet's ordinary stock held by state industrial holding company IRI cannot go ahead until parliament approves legislation setting up a regulatory authority to police the telecommunications sector.
Government ministers are set to meet representatives from the hard-left Communist Refoundation party on Friday to try to break the stalemate over the Stet sale.

Refoundation, which guarantees the government's majority in the lower chamber of parliament, opposes the Stet privatisation on ideological grounds. The party has tabled hundreds of amendments to the government draft law for the establishment of the regulatory authority.
Refoundation leader Fausto Bertinotti said on Friday he was unswerving in his opposition to a sell-off to private investors of the telecoms group, the fourth largest in Europe.
"We are against privatisation," Bertinotti told reporters. "We continue to favour the French model with the maintenance of 51 percent in public hands."
The French government has said it plans to sell 49 percent of state-owned France Telecom with a 20 percent block of shares being put up for sale next April.

The draft law is "closed in a draw at the Public Works committee of the Senate," said Turin daily La Stampa. "And short of a miracle it will remain there for a long time without the possibility of it being examined," added the newspaper.
Government officials are still standing by an official timetable of getting the privatisation off the ground by the end of March 1997 or shortly thereafter.

Vincenzo Vita, under secretary at the Post and Telecommunication ministry, denied an Italian news agency report on Thursday quoting him as saying that time had run out to get the privatisation through by March.
A delay beyond March would force the government to put the sale on ice at least until autumn because of Europe's crowded privatisation agenda next year.

Italy is under pressure to cash in on a Stet sale as quickly as possible to head off a fresh crisis at IRI, which is heading for losses of up to three trillion lire ($2 billion) this year and groaning under a debt load of 22.5 trillion lire.
Under a 1993 accord with the European Union, IRI must cut its debt to below five trillion lire, a target now seen as all but impossible to meet.
The government's task of forging ahead with the privatisation has been made no easier by objections from within its ranks to resorting to a firesale of Stet's assets.
"You cannot sell a company which is worth less than the shares that it has in its portfolio," said Defence Minister Beniamino Andreatta.

Stet, which is already listed on the Milan bourse, has a market value lower than the combined worth of its shareholdings in its two main operating companies, fixed line operator Telecom Italia and mobile phone group Telecom Italia Mobile.
